artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G$ be a finite abelian group and let $S \subseteq G$. The addition Cayley graph (also called the sum graph) induced on $G$ by $S$ is the graph with vertex set $G$ and edge set $\{\{g_1, g_2\} : g_1, g_2 \in G,\ g_1 + g_2 \in S\}$ (loops, where applicable, are ignored). 

Now restrict to the case where $G = \mathbb{Z}/n\mathbb{Z}$ is a finite cyclic group and $S \subseteq G$ is a $4$-element subset such that the induced addition Cayley graph is connected (equivalently, $S$ is not contained in a single coset of any proper subgroup of $G$, with at most a standard exception when $|G|$ is even). 

Prove or disprove: every such connected addition Cayley graph on a finite cyclic group induced by a $4$-element subset is Hamiltonian.
